To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have proposed an improved source counting and separation for monaural mixture.
we propose a novel single model for multi speaker separation with the number of speakers unknown, which can be trained in an end-to-end manner and achieves state of the art results.
we have developed a novel model of multi-speaker speech separation which can automatically count and separate the number of speakers.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following aspects of the problem: 1. How to count the number of speakers in monaural mixture. 2. How to improve the separation performance of monaural mixture with unknown number of speakers in a single model.

the following questions: How can we jointly model time and frequency features to better capture the characteristics of speech signals in single channel mixture? How can we count the number of speakers and separate them from the mixture? Can we learn to separate multiple speakers in a single model?
the following questions: 1. How can we jointly model time frequency representation and the unknown number time frequency representation and count the number of speakers in a single model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our method achieves the state of the arts in both source counting and separation performance on the GRID dataset.
the proposed method is able to achieve state of the art performance in single channel multi speaker speech separation, while simultaneously providing an estimation of the number of speakers.
the proposed model can accurately estimate and separate the speakers in a single channel mixture with a single model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose a novel framework for single channel multi speaker mixture separation, which can simultaneously count the number of speakers, separate the speakers, and recover the original waveform with only a single model.
we propose a novel single channel multi speaker speech separation model with a joint learning scheme for both the feature representation and the number of speakers.
we propose a novel method to count and separate the speakers from monaural mixture.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single model can be trained to count the number of speakers in the mixture and separate the speakers with a high accuracy.
the proposed model can be applied for real world applications with unknown number of speakers, which is a more practical setting in real life.
a single model can be used to jointly learn the time frequency representation, the unknown number of speaker and the separation of multi speaker mixtures.
